summary: The core of the design fits the code as it stands. Every refusal sits inside one of the four existing single statements (postSQL, Cast's INSERT…SELECT, which keeps its WHERE, Withdraw's DELETE, and sendSQL). Block and Unblock are one statement each. The read side already hides, counts and restores. TestPostRoutesAreClassified will force a body class for the new no-field POSTs. One required item is missing and it has real consequences: lesson #977's m5 was deferred to SC-021, and the design gives no remove control on the Blocked users page. moderationList shows only comments readers can see, and placeholders never get a remove form, so the owner has no way to remove a blocked account's comment while it is blocked. Unblocking then brings every one of them back, and the design's own test 6 assumes a removal that the UI cannot make. Smaller issues: m6 (ParentRemoved and its 'removed comment' wording) is still not picked up. The check that refuses to block the owner lives in one handler, while the fitness rule says Block does it. The error path of the follow-up EXISTS read is unstated. The tests the design says to flip are the wrong ones. The Blocked page's parent link goes nowhere for parents below the depth cap of 5 and for unpublished reports. The rule text about reads of blocked_accounts would become false. Extras for the backlog: a census so that any new participant write must be refused for blocked accounts, a Block entry point for accounts that only send feedback, a real-browser render of the owner UI, and a size limit on the Blocked page. I made no web searches: the design leans on no recalled outside claim. Its SQLite upsert and ServeMux GET/HEAD assumptions are long-standing, and Cast keeps the WHERE clause that the upsert parse needs.

findings.claim: The Blocked users page has no remove control. Lesson #977 (m5, deferred to SC-021 in SL-010's decision records) requires one per comment that is not yet removed, with a new strict `from` value, and the design leaves it out. Without it nothing in the UI can remove a blocked account's comment while it is blocked. moderationList shows only comments readers can see, so blocked comments drop off /admin/reports/<slug>. The reader-side CanRemove is false on placeholders. A blocked comment with no visible reply is drawn nowhere. So when the owner reviews a blocked account's comments and unblocks it, every one comes back publicly, abusive ones included. The only workaround is to unblock (publishing them), remove, then block again. The design's own test 6 ('A comment removed while its writer was blocked stays hidden after unblock') assumes a removal that only a hand-made POST can make.
findings.evidence: internal/server/thread.go:106 (moderationList emits only non-placeholder nodes); internal/server/admin.go:274-281 (the from enum accepts only absent or "admin"); design component '[SC-021] Block routes and the Blocked users page' lists each li with body, report link and parent link only; lesson #977 (1).
findings.fix: On admin_blocked.html, give each comment that is not removed the same `<details class="remove">` two-step, posting to /admin/comments/<id>/remove with a hidden from=blocked. Extend adminCommentRemove's enum with "blocked", landing on /admin/blocked (still built from nothing in the request), and add from=blocked rows to TestCommentRemove's from shapes and to the removeBodyRows corpus. TestUnblockRestores (test 6) must press that real remove form while the account is blocked and then the real POST /admin/users/<u>/unblock, not a SQL DELETE (lesson #977 (3), Q-026).

findings.claim: Once SC-021 can block accounts, a placeholder can mean 'blocked' as well as 'removed'. The admin moderation list still labels every reply under a placeholder 'in reply to a removed comment'. For a blocked parent that is false, and unblocking brings the parent back. Lesson #977 (2), m6, names this as SC-021's work, and the design does not pick it up.
findings.evidence: internal/server/thread.go:83-85 and :113 set ParentRemoved for any placeholder parent. internal/server/remove_test.go:648 and :704 pin the wording.

quote.text: {{if .ParentRemoved}}in reply to a removed comment{{else if .ParentLogin}}in reply to @{{.ParentLogin}}{{else}}top level{{end}}

findings.fix: Rename modItem.ParentRemoved to ParentHidden. Draw 'in reply to a hidden comment' (it keeps the block away from the word 'comment' beside a digit, as now), and update the two remove_test.go expectations to the observed new text.

findings.claim: The rule 'the owner cannot be blocked' depends on every caller remembering it. The design puts the auth.IsOwner check in the POST /admin/users/{u}/block handler only, and comments.Book.Block(ctx, u) is a bare INSERT. comments.Book is built from (db, now) and has no owner id, so it cannot refuse. The fitness rule fencing blocked_accounts justifies itself by saying the refusal lives in Block. Any later caller of Block, such as a Block form on feedback articles or a bulk block, can block the author. That would hide every Author comment on the site and refuse the owner's own posts with 403.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:434-436; internal/comments/comments.go:55-64 (Book{db, now}, New(db, now)); design '[SC-021] Block routes': 'auth.IsOwner(a.cfg.OwnerGitHubID, u): 400'.

quote.text: because: Block and Unblock in internal/comments are where the pinned owner's own id is refused,

findings.fix: Make Block refuse the owner itself: Block(ctx, ownerID, u) returning a new comments.ErrOwnerBlock when auth.IsOwner(ownerID, u), checked before the INSERT. The handler maps it to 400. TestBlock asserts the refusal at store level as well as through the route.

findings.claim: The design adds a follow-up `SELECT EXISTS (… blocked_accounts …)` after a 0-row write in Post, Cast, Withdraw and Send. It says 'the read only chooses the wording' and gives no result for a failed read. For Withdraw, which today never looks at RowsAffected and returns nil, a builder could reasonably return nil on a read error. A blocked account's withdraw would then get the success 303 although nothing happened, and a store fault would be hidden as success. Post, Cast and Send could equally fall back to ErrNoTarget or ErrNotOpen (404) on a read error.
findings.evidence: Design '[SC-021] Refusal at the point of use': 'When 0 rows are written, a follow-up read … picks the error … otherwise: the existing answer (ErrNoTarget, ErrNotOpen, or nil for a no-op Withdraw)'.

quote.text: `DELETE FROM votes WHERE report_id = ? AND github_id = ?`, reportID, githubID); err != nil {

findings.fix: State the contract: if the follow-up read fails, it returns a wrapped error ('votes: withdraw: is blocked: %w' and likewise for the others), which the handlers answer 503, never the existing refusal or nil. Give each package one unit case where the read fails, for example a ctx cancelled between the Exec and the read, or the read run against a closed pool.

findings.claim: The design tells the builder to flip 'the blocked-row cases near comment_test.go:448 and :1082'. Those cases only plant block rows, and the build check measured that they keep passing. The tests that actually break are elsewhere. One is the subtest at internal/server/branch_test.go:443-457, which expects a 303 for a blocked account's post. The other is the TestThreadCapFive fixture, which inserts the block row at :105 and then calls h.book().Post as account 9 under t.Fatal at :111. Once Post refuses, that fixture dies, and TestThreadCapFive is a depth-cap test, not a block test.

quote.text: if _, err := h.book().Post(bg, rep, 9, c[4], "C-hidden-6-end"); err != nil {

findings.fix: Name the real tests. In TestThreadCapFive, post C-hidden-6-end before inserting the blocked_accounts row (the reply is still hidden, which is what the fixture needs). Rewrite the 'a comment nobody can see keeps the report page' subtest as a 403-and-nothing-stored case at depths 0, 1 and cap+3.

findings.claim: On the Blocked users page, the link to the parent a reply answered is fixed as `/reports/<slug>#comment-<parent>`. That anchor is missing for any parent deeper than threadDepthCap (5), because such a parent is drawn only on a branch page, /reports/<slug>/comments/<root>. Blocked() also lists comments on drafts and unpublished reports (no status filter), and for those both the report link and the parent link go to a 404. The brief asks the page to show 'each hidden comment's report and parent comment'. For deep threads and unpublished reports the design's links show neither.
findings.evidence: internal/server/thread.go:17-20 (writes at any depth, drawn on branch pages); internal/server/comment.go:111 landing() already picks the branch page for an id via a.tree + Find + branchRoot; design '[SC-021] Block store' Blocked(): 'LEFT JOIN reports', with no status.
findings.fix: Build the parent link the way landing() does: one a.tree read per report shown on the page, then Find and branchRoot for the parent. Keep 'comment-<parent>' in the href so finish line 2's reader still matches. For a report that is not published, link to /admin/reports/<slug> instead of /reports/<slug>. Blocked() returns the report's status for this.

findings.claim: The design adds reads of blocked_accounts that the fitness rule's stated contract does not allow: a standalone `SELECT EXISTS` after a refused write in votes and in feedback, and an EXISTS column in feedback's inboxSQL. The rule's `because` says votes and feedback read the table only inside their own write statements. The regex fires only on writes, so nothing fails, but the rule then states something about the code that is false. This repeats the bounded_by drift lesson #969 records.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:437-438; design '[SC-021] Refusal at the point of use' and '[SC-021] Feedback: the blocked mark'.

quote.text: votes and feedback may only READ the table, inside their own write statements

findings.fix: Change the rule's because to the reads the design adds: NOT EXISTS inside writes, the post-refusal EXISTS read, and the owner inbox's blocked column. Keep it single-quoted and run Fitness op=check (lesson #971).

findings.claim: 'A blocked account cannot take part' depends on someone remembering it. It is four hand-placed copies of `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM blocked_accounts k WHERE k.github_id = ?)` in three packages, plus three follow-up reads. TestBlockedRefusals hand-lists six attempts on the three public POST routes. The router registers those routes with bare mux.HandleFunc calls and no table, so a later participant write would pass every test while letting a blocked account through. Examples are a sender's reply on a feedback thread (lesson #965 mentions SenderThreads) or a comment edit.
findings.evidence: internal/server/router.go:97-103 (the three public POST routes, hand-registered); design case 2 lists the six attempts by hand.
findings.fix: Give TestBlockedRefusals a census, as TestPostRoutesAreClassified is for adminRoutes. Keep a table of every non-admin POST pattern with its blocked-refusal case, and fail when the server answers a POST outside /admin and /auth that the table does not list. Probe this through the built mux, or refactor the three public writes into a route table the test enumerates.

findings.claim: The only Block entry point is the Block form on the moderation list. That list shows only comments readers can see. An account that only sends private feedback (abusive messages in the owner's inbox), or whose visible comments were all removed, has no Block control anywhere in the UI, although the brief says a block stops it sending feedback. Reaching it needs a hand-made POST with a numeric id the UI never shows.
findings.evidence: Design key decision '[SC-021] Block forms appear only on the admin moderation list'; the feedback-<n> articles on admin_report.html get only the 'blocked' badge.
findings.fix: Put a Block two-step in each feedback-<n> article of a sender who is not blocked, worded so that the lowercase word 'blocked' stays out of non-blocked articles: 'Block @login' contains no 'blocked'. It needs Message.GitHubID.

findings.claim: Owner UI is again planned without a real-browser render. That includes the Block `<details>` two-step on the moderation list, the Blocked users page, and the Unblock form, plus the remove form M1 adds. These are a fourth slice of signed-in owner controls proven only by httptest markup checks. The same-origin form POST through http.CrossOriginProtection from a real browser's Sec-Fetch-Site has never run (lessons #978, #961).
findings.evidence: Design 'How tests show it' lists only go tests and the HTTP-level finish lines 1 and 2.
findings.fix: One Go test that seeds an owner session through the test store, renders /admin/reports/<slug> and /admin/blocked in the engine's Chrome (TestReportScriptsNeverRun's harness), and checks that the Block and Unblock forms are closed by default and that the page is not blank.

findings.claim: /admin/blocked lists every comment and every feedback message of every blocked account, with no limit. With M1 it also carries one remove form per comment. The accounts most likely to be blocked are prolific spammers, which is the per-comment-form size problem lesson #960 measured (about 2.1 MB of forms at 10,000 comments). The design does not decide whether a limit applies, which lesson #966 asked owner pages to do.
findings.evidence: Design '[SC-021] Block routes and the Blocked users page': 'a <ul> with one <li> per comment'.
findings.fix: Decide it explicitly: either state that no limit applies, as the owner inbox does, or cap each account's section at its newest N comments with a count of the rest.

dimensions_checked.result: Checked the design's claims about the tree. visibleSQL reads blocked_accounts (comments.go:70). postSQL, Cast, Withdraw and sendSQL are single statements, and Cast's INSERT…SELECT keeps its WHERE when the predicate is added. The Owner(Inbox|Reply) fence covers OwnerInboxBySender. Raw-SQL block rows in TestCountReconciles and remove_test do not go through Post, so they survive the refusal. One wrong assumption: the tests to flip are named incorrectly (m4).

Parent links go nowhere below depth cap 5 and on unpublished reports (m5). Accounts that only send feedback cannot be blocked from the UI (m8). The page has no size limit (m10). Race between the refused write and the follow-up read: harmless, only the wording changes. Blocking an id that never signed in and repeated blocks are both covered.
The participant refusal is four hand-placed predicates with no census over public POST routes (m7). The owner refusal sits only in the handler (m2).
none: the follow-up EXISTS read is needed so Withdraw can tell a refusal from 'held no vote'. N+1 OwnerInboxBySender calls are proportionate for a one-person site. No new tables or migrations.

The follow-up read has no error contract (m3). Body policy for the field-less block and unblock POSTs (lesson #973) holds by construction: TestPostRoutesAreClassified (remove_body_corpus_test.go:160-185) fails on any unclassified adminRoutes POST, and its existing 'no field' class (publish/unpublish/delete) is the right one, so no finding.

m3: what a failed follow-up EXISTS read returns is not specified. Otherwise Block and Unblock errors give 500, GET /admin/blocked errors give 500 and never an empty page, and the handlers map ErrBlocked to 403. CC-002 was checked: no new PublishedBySlug-style lookups are added.

Lesson #977's deferred obligations: the m5 remove form on the Blocked page is missing (M1), and the m6 ParentRemoved rename is missing (m1). Test 6 must drive the real Unblock and remove routes (folded into M1). The built modItem lacks GitHubID and ParentID, which the design already intends SC-021 to add.

The fitness rule says Block refuses the owner, but the design puts that check in the handler (m2). The rule's prose on reads becomes false (m6). The ViewerFrom rule is unaffected: the handlers already use auth.Participant, and admin.go is exempt. The blocked_accounts write regex stays quiet on the votes and feedback statements, because \S* cannot span 'votes …'.

The design names tests TestBlock, TestBlockedRefusals, TestBlockedPage and TestUnblockRestores, plus observe() and TestFeedbackDoesNotInterfere rows, and both epic-44 bodies. Gaps: the wrong tests named to flip (m4), no real-route remove while blocked (M1), no failed-read case (m3), no real-browser render (m9). check_e006_1_stops_at_block.py has to go once line 1 passes (lesson #976); the design does not say this, and the build will find it.

The block, unblock and blocked-page routes sit behind RequireOwner, OwnerRoute and CrossOriginProtection. GitHubID appears only on admin pages. Removed bodies are blanked in SQL on the Blocked page. Private feedback reads stay inside the Owner* fence. The only weakness is that the owner refusal is not enforced at the store (m2). Unblock has no owner check, so self-blocking is recoverable.

verdicts.checked: internal/server/admin.go:273-295 (the from enum and the landing switch `case toAdmin || !published:`). internal/server/remove_body_corpus_test.go:43-116 (the bodyRow fields and how TestCommentRemoveBodyShapes works out the landing). internal/server/remove_test.go:365-404 (TestCommentRemove's landing table and the draft/unpublished landing cases). remove_body_corpus_test.go:160-185 (the TestPostRoutesAreClassified class for /remove).
verdicts.why: The fix's direction is right, and the rest of it can be built. Two gaps remain. (1) The corpus cannot take from=blocked rows as written. bodyRow's last field is a bool, and TestCommentRemoveBodyShapes turns it into one of only two landings (remove_body_corpus_test.go:97-101: `loc := "/reports/x#comments"; if c.admin { loc = "/admin/reports/x#comments" }`). A from=blocked 303 row would therefore assert the wrong Location whichever way the bool is set. (2) The fix says from=blocked lands on /admin/blocked, but it does not say this beats the existing `toAdmin || !published` branch. Blocked() lists comments on drafts and unpublished reports. A builder who appends `case fromBlocked:` after that branch sends a removal pressed on the Blocked users page for a draft's comment to /admin/reports/<slug>#comments. No row in the prescribed tests covers that combination. The rest holds: the landing is built from nothing in the request, the strict parse in removeFrom is unchanged, and the census class 'optional: from (removeBodyRows)' still applies. One thing is unverified: whether finish line 2's reader of the /admin/blocked li text tolerates the 'Remove' / 'Remove for everyone' text inside each not-removed li. I could not read the epic-44 body, because no shell was available for the read-only SELECT.
verdicts.instead: Change bodyRow's landing from `admin bool` to a landing string (or a three-way enum) and add the from=blocked urlencoded and multipart rows with Location /admin/blocked. In adminCommentRemove, make the from=blocked case come first: it lands on /admin/blocked whatever the report's status. Add TestCommentRemove landing rows for from=blocked on a published report, on an unpublished one and on a draft, plus 'from=Blocked' (400) and 'from=admin&from=blocked' (400). Run finish line 2 against the built page before closing the build.

verdicts.checked: internal/server/thread.go:72-125 (modItem, where ParentRemoved is set at :113 for any placeholder parent). internal/server/templates/admin_report.html:46. A grep of internal/ for ParentRemoved and 'removed comment': the only uses are thread.go, the template and remove_test.go:648/:704. tests/acceptance/check_e006_1_stops_at_block.py:4-9: finish line 1 reads reader pages, not the admin moderation list.
verdicts.why: The rename touches only the struct, one template line and two test expectations. The new wording 'in reply to a hidden comment' contains no 'blocked' (so it cannot trip the 'blocked only inside a blocked sender's feedback-<n>' reader), and it adds no digit beside 'comment'. It is also true in both cases. For a blocked parent, unblocking brings it back, which 'removed' would wrongly deny. For a removed parent it is still accurate. Reader-page placeholder text is not touched.

verdicts.checked: internal/auth/owner.go:20-22 (IsOwner). The internal/auth imports (config, store only, so comments→auth makes no cycle). The fitness.yaml must_not_import rules (nothing bars comments from importing auth). internal/server/router.go:71-73 (comments.New(st.DB(), clock), the only production constructor). internal/comments/comments.go:55-64.
verdicts.why: Moving the check into Block is right, but a per-call ownerID parameter still leaves the rule depending on the caller. Any int64 compiles. auth.IsOwner(ownerID, u) is `ownerID > 0 && githubID == ownerID`, so a caller passing 0 (a test fixture, a zero-value config, a new helper that forgets the config) gets false and Block proceeds: the store fails open. The rule 'the owner cannot be blocked' still rests on every caller supplying the right value, which is the class the finding was about.
verdicts.instead: Bind the owner id when the Book is built, by construction: comments.New(db, now, ownerID), set at router.go:72 from a.cfg.OwnerGitHubID, with the test fixtures updated mechanically. Block then refuses with ErrOwnerBlock when u == b.ownerID, and fails closed with an error when b.ownerID <= 0, never treating that as 'nobody is the owner'. TestBlock asserts both refusals at store level and the 400 through the route.

verdicts.checked: internal/votes/votes.go:53-84 (Cast and Withdraw: one ExecContext on b.db, no seam). internal/comments/comments.go:54-64 and :91-116 (Book{db, now}, Post). The CC-002 check in this project's reviewer lessons. A grep for an existing seam in the store packages: none, only a.tree in server.
verdicts.why: The contract is now right: a failed follow-up read gives a wrapped error and a 503, never the existing refusal or nil, and all three handlers already answer 503 for other errors. But neither example test can be built to test it. A closed pool makes the ExecContext fail first ('sql: database is closed'), so the test covers the existing 'votes: cast: %w' path and passes without any follow-up-read code. That is exactly the shadowing CC-002 records across three handlers. 'A ctx cancelled between the Exec and the read' has no hook: Book holds only db and now, and both calls happen inside one method. Dropping or renaming blocked_accounts fails the write too, because its NOT EXISTS names the table. So, as written, the read-failure branch ships untested and nothing would show it.
verdicts.instead: Add an unexported seam per Book, for example `isBlocked func(ctx context.Context, githubID int64) (bool, error)`, set in New to the real EXISTS read and replaced in each package's internal test. The unit case makes the write refuse (a blocked row, or an unpublished report for Post/Cast/Send) with the seam returning an error, and asserts a wrapped non-sentinel error: not errors.Is ErrBlocked, ErrNoTarget or ErrNotOpen, and not nil for Withdraw. Add one handler case per route asserting a 503 with nothing stored.

verdicts.checked: internal/server/branch_test.go:100-153 (TestThreadCapFive: the block row at :105, chains a/b/c/e grown by account 7, Post as 9 at :111, the assertions read only that the hidden reply and 'blocked-nine' are not drawn) and :443-457. internal/server/comment_test.go:439-471 (TestCommentParentRefused posts as reader/owner only after the block), :722-809 (only the reader posts after the block). internal/comments/comments_test.go:310-377 (byBlocked posted before the block, every refusal posted as account 1). internal/comments/remove_test.go:179-209 (posts as 8 only while unblocked). internal/server/remove_test.go:259-275. comment_test.go:1082 is raw SQL.
verdicts.why: Every test that plants a block row was checked for a later post as the blocked account. Only the two the fix names do it. Moving the INSERT at branch_test.go:105 to after :113 changes nothing else: chains a, b, c and e are written by account 7, and the later assertions need only C-hidden-6-end to be hidden, which the block row still does when it lands after the Post. The :443 subtest rewritten as a 403-and-nothing-stored case at parents 0, chain[0] and chain[cap+2] is what the slice asks for. Vote and feedback tests plant no block rows.

verdicts.checked: internal/server/comment.go:111-122 (landing: a.tree, then comments.Find, then branchRoot, falling back to /reports/<slug>#comment-<id>). internal/server/thread.go:138-148 (branchRoot: a nil path has depth 0 and returns nil). internal/comments/comments.go:11-18 (a hidden comment with nothing visible below it is dropped from the tree). The design's admin_report.html decision: 'no element whose id is comment-<n>'.
verdicts.why: Three gaps. (1) a.tree returns the pruned forest. When the parent is itself hidden (removed, or written by a blocked account, very often the same blocked account answering itself) and the blocked reply is the only thing under it, the parent is dropped. Find then returns nil, and landing's logic quietly falls back to /reports/<slug>#comment-<parent> even when the parent sits below the cap. The fix does not say what the link is in that case, or that the page should show that the parent is not publicly visible. (2) For a report that is not published, the fix keeps comment-<parent> in an /admin/reports/<slug>#comment-<parent> href, but the admin page deliberately draws no comment-<n> ids, so that anchor never exists. The parent cannot be found there either, because moderationList leaves hidden parents out. (3) a.tree takes a report id, and Blocked() as designed returns only Slug and Title. The fix adds status but not the id the tree read needs. One thing is unverified: whether finish line 2 matches the parent href exactly or only by containing comment-<parent>. The build check describes it as 'a comment-<parent> link', but the epic-44 body was not readable here.
verdicts.instead: Blocked() returns ReportID and Status per comment. GET /admin/blocked does one a.tree per distinct published report, with a 500 on error as for the rest of the page. For a parent that Find locates, use branchRoot's page with #comment-<parent>. For a parent that Find does not locate (hidden, nothing visible below), draw the li's parent reference as text, 'in reply to a hidden comment', with no anchor link. For a report that is not published, link the report to /admin/reports/<slug> and give the parent reference as text, not a #comment-<parent> anchor the page never draws. TestBlockedPage covers a parent below the cap, a hidden parent and a draft.

verdicts.checked: .taad/fitness.yaml:430-441 (the rule's because is a plain multi-line scalar, not quoted). Lesson #971 (go test's loadRules accepts invalid YAML, and the engine's Fitness op=check rejects the whole file). The regex at :433, which stays quiet on reads, so no corpus rows change.
verdicts.why: The need is real, but the instruction 'keep it single-quoted' describes a state the file is not in: the because at :434-438 is an unquoted plain scalar. A builder who 'keeps' its style and writes the new list of reads with a colon, for example 'the reads it allows: NOT EXISTS inside writes, …', produces a plain scalar containing ': '. That is invalid YAML, which go test still passes and the engine rejects whole (#971). The text must also stay true with m2: 'Block and Unblock in internal/comments are where the pinned owner's own id is refused' becomes true only once m2 moves the refusal into the store.
verdicts.instead: Rewrite the because as a single-quoted scalar, with apostrophes doubled (for example 'owner''s'). List the three read shapes: NOT EXISTS inside the write statements of votes and feedback, the follow-up EXISTS read after a refused write, and the blocked column of feedback's owner inbox. Keep the sentence about where the owner refusal lives in step with how m2 is built. Run the engine's Fitness op=check, not only go test, before leaving the build.

prescribed.summary: Seven prescriptions checked against the tree. m1 and m4 hold. In m4 I checked every test that plants a block row: only branch_test.go:105-111 and :443-457 post as a blocked account. TestCommentParentRefused, the comments package tests and the server's remove/count tests post as that account only before the block or after the unblock. The other five have holes. M1: the removeBodyRows corpus records the landing as a two-valued `admin bool`, so from=blocked rows cannot be added as written. It also never says that from=blocked must take precedence over the existing 'not published goes to the admin report page' branch. m2: Block(ctx, ownerID, u) fails open on ownerID <= 0, because auth.IsOwner returns false there, so the rule still holds only if every caller remembers it. m3: neither suggested test (a closed pool, a ctx cancelled between the Exec and the read) can make only the follow-up read fail.
